intro.text: 今天的主线很清楚：agent 正在变成新的互联网本身。Microsoft CTO Kevin Scott 在播客里给出一个漂亮的类比——MCP 之于 agent，就像 HTTP 之于网站，未来每一个有网站、有 API 的服务，都得想清楚怎么让 agent 能「对话」它。同一天，Claude 的会话开始在 Chrome、桌面、Web、手机之间漫游，Steinberger 观察到 agent 的形态一年内从 CLI 走到 app，再走到云端服务。而 Levie 用 Jevons 悖论解释 DeepSeek 和 Grok 的降价：越便宜，需求反而越大。最后留一条轻松的：Askell 在 Skyrim 里找到了不杀生的通关方式，还收养了孤儿。

sections.title: The Model Price Crash / 模型降价潮
sections.desc: DeepSeek 和 Grok 的新模型把能力又推高一截，价格却低得离谱。Levie 说这是 AI 的 Jevons 悖论：越便宜，需求反而加速膨胀。

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie calls it an awesome day for AI economics: new model releases from both DeepSeek and Grok represent huge jumps in capability at insanely low costs, and he sees this as Jevons paradox playing out for AI in real time—bringing down the cost doesn't shrink demand, it accelerates it.

His evidence from the field: enterprises have vastly more use-cases they'd like agents to handle than they can budget for today. They want agents scanning codebases for security issues, reviewing all their documents, processing information across large parts of their workflows. Lower cost opens up exactly those use cases, which drives even greater demand.

His kicker for builders: this is also great for the applied AI layer. The more model choice there is—especially models tuned for different types or costs of work—the more value sits in the layer that can route and optimize based on the task. Good for the entire stack.
original: Awesome day in terms of new model releases from both Deepseek and Grok. Both of these new model updates represent huge jumps in capability at insanely low costs.

This is truly Jevons paradox for AI playing out. By bringing down the cost of AI, demand will continue to accelerate. When I talk to enterprises, they have vastly more use-cases for what they'd like agents to handle than generally what they're able to budget for today.

They want agents to scan their codebases for security issues. They want agents to review all their documents. They want agents to process information in a large portion of their workflows. And so on. When we bring down the cost of AI or drive up capability levels, it opens up all new use cases in the enterprises, which drives even greater demand.

This is also great for the applied AI layer. The more choice of models - especially those tuned for different types (or costs) of work - the more value there is in being at the layer that can route and optimize based on the task. Great for the entire stack right now.

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie 说今天是 AI 经济学的「awesome day」：DeepSeek 和 Grok 的新模型都是能力大跳进，价格却低得离谱。他认为这是 Jevons 悖论在 AI 身上真实上演——把成本打下来，需求不会萎缩，反而会加速膨胀。
他的一线证据：企业想交给 agent 的用例，远远多过他们现在的预算。他们想让 agent 扫代码库查安全问题、审阅所有文档、处理大量工作流里的信息。成本降下来，这些用例就全部打开了，然后需求继续上涨。
他给 builder 的收尾：这对应用层也是大利好。模型选择越多——尤其是针对不同类型/成本的工作调优的模型——能按任务做路由和优化的那一层价值就越大。整个栈都在受益。

这是 AI 的 Jevons 悖论：成本下降，需求加速。企业想用 agent 干的活远多于现有预算。
扫代码库安全、审阅文档、处理工作流……成本一降，这些用例全打开，需求继续涨。
对应用层也是大利好：模型选择越多，做路由和优化的层价值越大。

rewrite: Madhu Guru makes the case that the biggest alpha in AI products over the next few years is in the application layer, not the models.

His logic: models will keep getting cheaper, better and more local, so differentiation has to come from deeply understanding specific user workflows and having the imagination to redesign the experience around them.
The uncomfortable part: the denominator of people who can build AI products is about to get enormous, so being in the top 0.1% of builders will matter more than ever.

sections.title: The Agentic Web, One Year In / Agent 互联网成形中
sections.desc: Microsoft CTO 说 MCP 之于 agent 就像 HTTP 之于网站；Claude 的会话开始在浏览器、桌面、手机之间漫游；agent 的形态一年内从 CLI 走到了云端服务。

rewrite: The Takeaway: the next web won't be built just for people—it will be built for agents, and MCP is its HTTP.

Microsoft CTO Kevin Scott, a 41-year programmer who still uses vi, argues that the 'agentic web' is this year's real story, replacing scaling-law hype. His core case: agents are only useful if they can take action across systems, so every service with a website or API needs to figure out how to plumb itself through so agents can talk to it. Simple open protocols like MCP play the same role HTTP played on the internet, and NL web is the moral equivalent of HTML.

He flags 'capability overhang' as the industry's real problem: model reasoning has gotten ahead of what products actually deliver to users, and closing that gap is the collective work ahead. On security, he argues MCP is so coherently simple that the community can converge on the right model—starting with agent identity and entitlements: an agent acts on behalf of a person, requests permission for the systems it needs to touch, and admins get a yes or no. Open, not proprietary.

Asked whether agents kill the craft of coding, he shrugs: makers have always had strong opinions about tools—'real woodworkers only use hand tools,' then power tools, now CNC. His advice: 'Be curious, try stuff, and if it works for you, use it. And if it doesn't, don't.' He regrets waiting forever to learn 3D printers; don't repeat that.

His prediction for a year out: agents go from synchronous to asynchronous. You'll hand off 'go sort this out,' the agent will spend hours calling systems, iterating, and come back with 'here's as far as I got—now it's your turn.'
original: if agents are gonna be useful, they have to take action on your behalf. They have to be able to use tools and make changes in systems and consult information sources that are diverse and rich. And in order for that to really be great, you need an ecosystem that looks a lot like the Internet.

you've seen the first glimmers of real progress with super awesome, simple open protocols like MCP that are serving the same purpose in this agentic web as HTTP does on the internet and where you have things like NL web that are serving the same moral equivalent purpose as HTML does on the internet.

the reasoning capabilities of the models has actually gotten a little bit ahead of what we're using the models to do in products. So I've been talking a lot lately about this thing called the capability overhang.
we need agents to have identities, so that you can build entitlement systems. So you can say this agent is acting on behalf of this person and they're entitled to see these resources in this system.
be curious, try stuff, and if it works for you, use it. And if it doesn't, don't.

by next year, you're going to see people using these agents to like, 'Hey, go sort this out.' And the agent is going to take a lot of time. It's going to go make a lot of calls out to systems... and then at some non trivial amount of time later, you're going to sort of say, okay, here's as far as I got, now it's your turn.

rewrite: 一句话总结：下一代的互联网不只是给人用的——它是给 agent 用的，而 MCP 就是它的 HTTP。

Microsoft CTO Kevin Scott，一个写了 41 年代码、至今还在用 vi 的老程序员，认为「agentic web」才是今年的真正故事，取代了 scaling law 的炒作。他的核心论证：agent 要有用，就必须能替你采取行动，所以每个有网站、有 API 的服务都得想清楚怎么把自己接进去，让 agent 能和它「对话」。像 MCP 这样简单开放的标准协议，扮演的正是 HTTP 在互联网里的角色，而 NL web 相当于 HTML 的道德等价物。
他点出行业真正的问题是「capability overhang」：模型的推理能力已经跑到了产品实际交付的前面，弥合这个差距是接下来整个行业的集体功课。说到安全，他认为 MCP 简单到足够连贯，社区完全能收敛出一个正确的安全模型——起点是 agent 的身份和授权体系：agent 代表某个人行事，向系统请求它需要的权限，管理员给 yes 或 no。开放，而不是私有。
被问到 agent 会不会毁掉 coding 的「手艺感」，他很松弛：maker 从来都对工具有强烈的意见——「真木工只用手动工具」到电动工具，再到 CNC。他的建议是：「保持好奇，去试。对你有用就用，没用就别用。」他后悔自己等了好久才学 3D 打印，别重蹈覆辙。
他对一年后的预测：agent 会从同步走向异步。你把「去把这事搞定」丢给它，它花几个小时调用各种系统、反复迭代，最后回来说：「我到这一步了，接下来轮到你。」
original: agent 要有用，就必须替你采取行动——能使用工具、改系统、查各种信息源。要做到这一点，你需要一个长得像互联网的生态。
MCP 这样的简单开放协议，在 agentic web 里扮演的就是 HTTP 在互联网里的角色；NL web 相当于 HTML。
模型的推理能力已经领先于产品实际交付的东西——这就是 capability overhang。
agent 需要身份，才能建授权体系：这个 agent 代表这个人行事，有权访问这些资源。
保持好奇，去试。对你有用就用，没用就别用。
明年你会看到：把「搞定这事」丢给 agent，它花大量时间调用系统、迭代，然后回来说「我到这一步了，轮到你」。

rewrite: Anthropic's big announcement of the day, with 8,533 likes: Claude in Chrome sessions now carry over to desktop, web, and mobile. Conversations are saved, and your skills and connectors work in the browser.

The side panel now runs the same Claude Cowork session as the desktop, web, and mobile apps—sessions live with your account, not on any single device, so you can start in a tab and pick it up later somewhere else.
The significance: this is the consumer-side manifestation of the agentic web Kevin Scott describes—your agent work follows you across every surface, with the browser as the hub.
Available on Max and Team today, rolling out to Pro in the coming weeks.

sections.title: Builder Infrastructure / Builder 的基础设施
sections.desc: GBrain 把个人 AGI 做成独立 agent + markdown 记忆；Turck 用一个梗点破 AI 工程圈每隔几个月就重新发明一次术语。

rewrite: Y Combinator President Garry Tan ships GBrain v0.45.6.0, adding 17 new brain skills 'hardened through my own personal OpenClaw agent with hundreds of thousands of markdown files.' His definition of a personal AGI: 'A personal AGI is one that works for you.' GBrain now works with Codex and Claude Code, too.

His architecture advice: run GBrain as a *separate agent*, not inside your main coding agent—think of it as a personal AI version of ChatGPT or Claude that has its own git repo for memory and custom skills.
And his stance on the substrate: 'We are gonna be markdown skill-maxxing from here'—plain markdown files as the durable memory layer for personal AI.

rewrite: FirstMark partner Matt Turck delivers the driest engineering take of the day: 'Graph engineering is the new loop engineering which is the new harness engineering which is the new context engineering which is the new prompt engineering. Hope this clarifies any confusion.'
It's a joke, but a real one: every few months the AI community renames the same underlying work, and the only honest response is a shrug and a 'hope this clarifies any confusion.'

rewrite: FirstMark 合伙人 Matt Turck 贡献了今天最干的一条工程梗：「Graph engineering 是新的 loop engineering，loop engineering 是新的 harness engineering，harness engineering 是新的 context engineering，context engineering 是新的 prompt engineering。希望这澄清了大家的困惑。」
这是玩笑，但也是真的：每隔几个月，AI 社区就把同一件底层工作换个名字，唯一诚实的回应就是耸耸肩，加一句「希望这澄清了大家的困惑」。

sections.title: Off-Hours / 休息时间
sections.desc: 今天的最后一课来自 Skyrim：不杀生也能通关，还能收养孤儿、给他们盖房子。

rewrite: Amanda Askell shares her Skyrim playstyle, and it's a small masterpiece: 'When I started playing Skyrim, I quickly realized you can make a lot of progress without doing any killing. You can also adopt orphans and build them nice houses, so I focused on that. I honestly don't really remember the plot beyond "that challenging fantasy philanthropy game".'

968 likes, because it's the rare player who turns an open-world RPG into an ethics sandbox—and picks the path where nobody gets hurt. Her follow-up on Bioshock is in the same spirit: 'The bar for "ethical" playthroughs is interesting. In Bioshock, the bar is literally not murdering children. Murdering adults is fine.'

The bar for "ethical" playthroughs of different games is interesting. In Bioshock, the bar is literally not murdering children. Murdering adults is fine.
